name: Butter Chicken
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi / Delhi, Moti Mahal-style murgh makhani)

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ½ cup (30 ml soaking + 100 ml blending/simmering)

equipment: Mixing bowl for marinating, with a lid or cling film
Heavy non-stick pan or tawa for searing the chicken
Kadai or heavy-bottomed pan (about 20 cm) for the gravy
Small bowl for soaking cashews (hot water from a kettle or small pan)
Spatula or wooden spoon, and tongs or a fork for turning chicken
Measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp is about 5 ml)
Optional sieve for a silky restaurant-smooth gravy

steps.title: Cut the chicken
steps.text: Cut 150 g boneless chicken thigh into 6–8 pieces of about 3 cm and trim off big fat bits.
steps.tip: wash hands, knife and board with soap straight after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: even-size pieces, no large white fat strips
steps.videoShot: knife slicing thigh into chunks
steps.watchOut: uneven pieces, where small ones overcook while big ones stay pink; cut them as close to the same size as you can.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Put the chicken in a bowl with 1 tsp lemon juice, ¼ tsp salt and ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and mix well.
steps.visualCue: every piece coated red
steps.videoShot: spoon tossing chicken in red spice
steps.watchOut: pale patches where no spice reached; toss again until none are left.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Add 2 tbsp (30 g) thick curd, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, a pinch of turmeric and ¼ tsp garam masala. Mix until every piece is covered.
steps.visualCue: thick, pale-orange coating clinging to the chicken, not runny
steps.videoShot: curd folded through the chicken
steps.watchOut: watery curd, which makes a thin liquid pooling in the bowl and chicken that steams instead of browning; hang the curd in a cloth or sieve for 15 min first.

steps.title: Rest the chicken
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave it in the fridge.
steps.visualCue: covered bowl on the fridge shelf
steps.videoShot: bowl covered and placed on the fridge shelf
steps.watchOut: leaving it on the counter, where raw chicken warms up unsafely; keep it cold the whole time.

steps.title: Soak cashews
steps.text: Put 10 g (7–8) cashews in a small bowl and cover with 30 ml hot water.
steps.visualCue: cashews look slightly swollen and softer
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of cashews submerged in water
steps.videoShot: hot water poured over cashews in a steel katori
steps.watchOut: throwing away the soaking water; you need it in step 21.

steps.title: Chop onion
steps.text: Roughly chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: rough 2 cm pieces; size does not matter because it all gets blended
steps.videoShot: knife cutting onion into chunks
steps.watchOut: tears and slipping; keep the cut side down on the board so the onion does not roll.

steps.title: Chop tomatoes
steps.text: Roughly chop 150 g (2 medium) tomatoes, removing the hard stem point.
steps.visualCue: juicy red chunks
steps.videoShot: tomatoes quartered and chopped
steps.watchOut: hard green stem bits, which stay woody after blending; cut them out.

steps.title: Set out gravy spices
steps.text: On a small plate put 1 cardamom pod (lightly crushed), 2 cloves, the 2 cm cinnamon piece, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp sugar, a big pinch of salt, a pinch of garam masala and ½ tsp kasuri methi, each in its own heap.
steps.visualCue: separate heaps of whole and ground spices
steps.videoShot: spoon placing each spice on the plate
steps.watchOut: looking for a spice with the pan already hot; once cooking starts there is no time to measure.

steps.title: Heat the searing pan
steps.text: Put the non-stick pan or tawa on medium-high heat and add 1 tsp (5 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers and flows freely
steps.videoShot: oil spreading across the hot pan
steps.watchOut: smoking oil, which means the pan is too hot; lower the heat for a moment.

steps.title: Lay in the chicken
steps.text: Place the chicken pieces in a single layer with space between them. Do not stir.
steps.visualCue: loud sizzle as each piece goes in
steps.cameraCheck: the pan with chicken spread out
steps.videoShot: chicken pieces placed one by one, sizzling
steps.watchOut: crowding, where the pieces touch and the chicken boils in its juices; use a bigger pan or sear in two rounds.

steps.title: Sear the first side
steps.text: Leave the chicken alone on medium-high.
steps.visualCue: underside is golden-brown with a few dark charred spots; pieces release easily from the pan
steps.cameraCheck: one piece lifted to show the browned side
steps.videoShot: tongs lifting a piece to show the char
steps.watchOut: tugging a piece that sticks; it is not ready, so wait another 30 seconds and it will let go.

steps.title: Sear the second side
steps.text: Turn each piece over and cook.
steps.visualCue: both sides browned; the inside is white with no pink when you cut the thickest piece
steps.cameraCheck: one piece cut open showing white meat
steps.videoShot: knife cutting a seared piece in half
steps.watchOut: cooking until dry and hard; stop at the first sign of no pink because the chicken finishes cooking in the gravy.

steps.title: Rest the chicken
steps.text: Move the chicken to a plate. Scrape any browned bits from the pan onto the plate too.
steps.visualCue: plate of charred, orange-red chicken
steps.videoShot: chicken tipped onto a steel plate
steps.watchOut: leaving the browned bits stuck to the pan, as they carry a lot of flavour.

steps.title: Melt butter for the gravy
steps.text: Put the kadai on low-medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) butter.
steps.visualCue: butter melted and foaming gently, not brown
steps.videoShot: butter melting and foaming
steps.watchOut: brown specks or a burnt smell, which mean the heat is too high; lower it before adding anything.

steps.title: Temper whole spices
steps.text: Add the cardamom, cloves and cinnamon.
steps.visualCue: spices sizzle; cloves puff slightly; warm, sweet smell
steps.videoShot: whole spices sizzling in butter
steps.watchOut: blackening spices, which turn bitter; move on to the onion straight away.

steps.title: Sauté onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: onion soft and translucent at the edges, not brown
steps.videoShot: onion stirred in foaming butter
steps.watchOut: browning, which darkens the gravy and loses the bright orange colour; lower the heat and splash 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add ½ tsp ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: raw garlic smell fades
steps.videoShot: paste stirred into onions
steps.watchOut: sticking and scorching; stir constantly and add a spoon of water if it grabs the pan.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and cashews
steps.text: Add the chopped tomatoes and the drained cashews (save the soaking water).
steps.visualCue: pan full of tomato chunks with cashews mixed through
steps.videoShot: tomatoes and cashews tipped in
steps.watchOut: pouring the soaking water down the sink; keep it in a cup.

steps.title: Cook tomatoes down
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low, stirring every minute or two.
steps.visualCue: tomatoes are completely mushy and break when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, pressing a tomato with the spatula
steps.videoShot: spatula squashing soft tomato
steps.watchOut: firm tomato pieces, which leave a raw sour taste; cook until you can crush a piece with the spatula.

steps.title: Remove whole spices and cool
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Pick out the cinnamon, cloves and cardamom, then tip the mixture onto a plate to cool.
steps.visualCue: warm, no longer steaming hard
steps.cameraCheck: the plate, with the whole spices set aside
steps.videoShot: tongs lifting out the cinnamon stick
steps.watchOut: blending while hot; steam can blow the lid off the jar. Leaving the whole spices in makes the gravy gritty.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Put the mixture in the small mixer jar with the saved cashew water and blend until completely smooth.
steps.visualCue: smooth, bright orange-red purée with no cashew flecks
steps.videoShot: purée pouring off a spoon in a smooth ribbon
steps.watchOut: gritty bits from under-blending; rub a drop between your fingers and blend longer if it feels grainy (a sieve fixes it too).

steps.title: Bloom the chilli
steps.text: Return the kadai to low heat (a little butter is left in it). Add ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and stir.
steps.visualCue: the fat turns deep red; smells toasty
steps.videoShot: red chilli swirling in the butter
steps.watchOut: a sharp burnt smell, which means the chilli has scorched and will turn the gravy bitter; keep the heat low and have the purée ready.

steps.title: Add purée
steps.text: Pour in the blended purée straight away and stir.
steps.visualCue: sauce bubbles gently and spits a little
steps.videoShot: purée poured into the red butter
steps.watchOut: splashes; stand back a little and keep the lid ready.

steps.title: Cook the gravy
steps.text: Cook on medium-low, partly covered, stirring often.
steps.visualCue: gravy darkens a shade, thickens, and small drops of fat appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pan edge showing fat separating
steps.videoShot: thick gravy bubbling with shiny edges
steps.watchOut: a raw tomato taste if cut short; wait for the fat to show at the edges.

steps.title: Season and loosen
steps.text: Add the sugar, salt and about 60–70 ml water. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
steps.visualCue: gravy coats the back of a spoon and drips slowly; taste is tangy, mildly sweet, mildly spicy
steps.cameraCheck: the back of the spoon coated in gravy
steps.videoShot: finger line drawn through gravy on a spoon
steps.watchOut: too thin or too thick; add water 1 tbsp at a time because it thickens as it simmers.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the seared chicken and any juices from the plate. Stir gently.
steps.visualCue: every piece coated in orange gravy
steps.videoShot: chicken folded into the gravy
steps.watchOut: breaking the pieces with hard stirring; fold, do not mash.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low so the chicken soaks up the gravy.
steps.visualCue: gravy bubbles lazily; chicken is hot right through
steps.videoShot: slow bubbles around the chicken pieces
steps.watchOut: a hard boil, which toughens the chicken; if the gravy gets too thick, add 1–2 tbsp water.

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: aroma becomes noticeably "restaurant-like"
steps.videoShot: kasuri methi crushed between palms
steps.watchOut: adding it too early, as the aroma cooks off; add it at the end.

steps.title: Add garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in a pinch of garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed
steps.videoShot: garam masala sprinkled over
steps.watchOut: a heavy hand; more than a pinch makes the gravy taste bitter and dusty.

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off. Swirl in 20 ml (1 heaped tbsp) fresh cream.
steps.visualCue: gravy turns a paler, glossy orange
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled through orange gravy
steps.watchOut: curdled white flecks, which mean the cream went into a boiling pan; always switch off the heat first.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Spoon into a bowl and top with chopped coriander (optional) and a tiny swirl of cream if you like.
steps.visualCue: glossy orange curry with charred chicken pieces showing
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the finished bowl
steps.watchOut: serving it piping hot straight from the pan; let it sit 1 minute so the gravy settles.

reasons: The home version is high in protein (~37 g) from chicken thigh and curd. The chicken is pan-seared in 1 tsp oil, not deep-fried, and the fat is moderate (~30 g) from 10 g butter, 20 ml cream and 10 g cashews. Saturated fat (about 57% of the daily limit) and sodium (about 53%) are the weak spots. Restaurant butter chicken typically uses several times the butter and cream, more sugar and salt, sometimes food colour, and comes with a butter naan, so a bowl can easily pass 700–900 kcal (est.).

researchRating.basis: one of India's best-known and most-loved dishes worldwide, with home recipes rated 4.9 or higher across several sites, and a legacy so valued that two Delhi restaurant families went to court over who invented it. The recurring criticism is that restaurant versions can be too sweet, too creamy or artificially coloured. The rating is unchanged from the last version.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 2 days (cool it within 1 hour of cooking). Freezer: up to 1 month (est.); the cream may separate slightly but comes back when you stir it while reheating. Reheating: gently on the stove on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, until steaming hot right through. In the microwave, use 1-minute bursts and stir in between. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Butter chicken toastie (Bombay-style grilled sandwich). Shred the leftover chicken into the thickened gravy, spread it on buttered bread with grated cheese, sliced onion and a smear of green chutney, then grill on a tawa until crisp (contains gluten from the bread).
burnOff: about 7 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 10 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).

navratri.reason: chicken, onion and garlic are all avoided in vrat

ekadashi.reason: chicken, onion and garlic are avoided (most common rule set assumed)

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root rule, Patch 05)

ramadan.reason: use halal-sourced chicken; rich and fairly salty (about 50% of the 2,000 mg sodium limit), so better as the main iftar dish than as sehri

jain.reason: chicken, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (a root) are all in the recipe

sattvik.reason: chicken is not sattvik, and the recipe uses onion and ginger-garlic paste

glutenFree.reason: chicken, curd, cashews, tomato and whole or ground spices; no wheat, rava, maida or hing (check the garam masala and chilli powder labels for fillers)

dairyFree.reason: curd 30 g, butter 10 g and cream 20 ml are dairy; use coconut yoghurt, oil and coconut cream (see Dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: the dish is defined by chicken, and the gravy is built on onion and ginger-garlic; a Jain version would be a different dish.
the dish is defined by chicken (plus butter, cream and curd); a plant-based makhani is a different dish.
Main recipe already gluten-free (no wheat, rava, maida or hing).
replacing the chicken gives butter paneer / Paneer Butter Masala (dish 3), a different dish.
